nodes.label: Lagrangian Relaxation (Lagrange gevsetmesi)
nodes.rationale: Relaxes only the edge-capacity constraint (load_e <= K) into the objective with multipliers lambda (harness_demo/routing/lagrangian.py); EMC separation is not part of this model. L(lambda) gives a lower bound on total cable length, a capacity-respecting repair heuristic gives the upper bound; the final gap is 0.002%.

nodes.label: CI Workflow (GitHub Actions)
nodes.rationale: Runs lint (ruff), type check (mypy), pytest and a no-image smoke run with --workers 2 on Python 3.11 so the parallel benchmark path is exercised on Linux where fork is cheap.

nodes.label: Viewer HTML Template
nodes.rationale: Placeholders (__STYLE__, __SCRIPT__, __DATA_JSON__, __THREE_VERSION__) are filled by presentation.py to produce a single self-contained docs/index.html working from Pages and file system.

nodes.label: Pinned Runtime Dependencies (requirements.txt)
nodes.rationale: Shortest-path tie-breaking varies between library versions (e.g. changes Lagrangian iteration count); exact pins keep python main.py reproducible.

nodes.label: Capacitated Steiner Forest
nodes.rationale: The real project's model: bundling represented directly in the objective with edge opening costs, solved with Lagrangian relaxation instead of heuristic discounts.

nodes.label: Headless Chrome Capture Mode
nodes.rationale: All README 3D images are captured from the interactive page itself (window.viewer API, driven via choreographer) so images match exactly what the page shows.

nodes.label: Edge Capacity K
nodes.rationale: K=2 is deliberately tight so the constraint is active; it lowers the bundling ratio of method e.

nodes.label: Independent Checks (checks.py)
nodes.rationale: checks.py imports no project module so verification does not depend on the routing code it verifies; keep-out volumes typed via a Protocol.

nodes.label: Keep-out Volumes and Clearance
nodes.rationale: Nodes inside grown volumes and edges crossing them are removed from the graph, so keep-out/clearance violations are zero by construction; a no-clearance baseline yields 69 violations to prove the check works.

nodes.label: Projected Subgradient with Polyak Step
nodes.rationale: When no feasible upper bound exists, target is best lower bound +5% so the step stays finite (previous version produced NaN multipliers).

nodes.label: Rip-up and Reroute
nodes.rationale: Sequential routing depends on cable order; rerouting conflicting cables while seeing all others, doubling EMC penalty each round, and returning the best seen solution reduces order dependence and never worsens the result.

nodes.label: Robustness Benchmark
nodes.rationale: A single zero-violation result of a sequential method can be luck; random order and terminal perturbation families (seed 7) measure order sensitivity. Parallel workers default 1 on Windows/macOS due to spawn cost.

nodes.label: Routes Export (routes.json)
nodes.rationale: Compact and deterministic (no timings) so it reproduces byte-for-byte and git shows only real changes; first step toward CAD export.

nodes.label: main.py run Pipeline (build_model -> route_all -> checks -> exports -> benchmark -> presentation)
nodes.norm_label: main.py run pipeline (build_model -> route_all -> checks -> exports -> benchmark -> presentation)

nodes.label: Bend-aware Turn Graph
nodes.rationale: States are directed edges; transitions exist only if circumradius >= min bend radius, the same condition the independent bend check tests, so bend violations are zero by construction (51,544 of 109,924 turns kept).

nodes.label: Wire Harness Routing Demo (English README)
nodes.rationale: Simplified prototype of EMC-aware aircraft wire harness routing on 3D fuselage geometry; goal is to show correct problem understanding and a testable modular skeleton, every result measured by checks independent of routing code.

nodes.label: c) EMC-aware Bundling
nodes.rationale: Soft EMC penalty on edges touching risky nodes (cKDTree neighbourhood); expensive but violable.

nodes.label: d) Simplified Lagrangian Relaxation
nodes.rationale: Relaxes capacity into the objective so problem decomposes into per-cable shortest paths giving a lower bound; a repair heuristic gives an upper bound. Simplified: no bundling or EMC in the model.

nodes.label: e) Integrated Method (EMC + capacity + bend)
nodes.rationale: Only method satisfying all five checks at once; runs c's bundling/EMC/rip-up logic on a bend-aware turn graph with near-hard capacity penalty (x1000).
